world.bio: I run a small gallery in Alfama devoted to indigenous textiles: backstrap weaving from the Andes, Maya huipiles, Sami band weaving, a few pieces from the Philippines. My Alfama gallery shows only indigenous textiles and prints every maker's name on the wall label, a rule that has cost me a few sales to people who wanted "anonymous folk art" and won me a loyal circle of collectors. Twenty-two years in textiles, eleven of them with this space.
skills_assets: A 70 square metre ground-floor gallery in Alfama with north light and a small back room for storage
Relationships with weaving cooperatives in Peru, Guatemala, Norway and Mindanao built over two decades
A mailing list of about 1,400 collectors, curators and interior designers
Conservation basics: mounting, humidity control, safe hanging for fragile textiles
Fluent Portuguese, English, Spanish; working French
A part-time assistant, Inês, who handles Instagram and shipping
Standing invitation as an exhibitor at Lisbon design week

projects.name: Autumn show: Quechua belts from Chinchero
projects.text: Twelve belts and three mantles from a women's group near Cusco, arriving in two shipments. The labels are written; each carries the weaver's name, village, year, and the dye plant if known. I am fighting with the printer over typeface: he keeps wanting to shrink the names to make the title bigger. Opening is 17 October.

projects.name: Design-week programme 2027
projects.text: The design-week committee confirmed my slot in May 2027. My May 2027 design-week slot opened up after an Andean weaving collective pulled out over visa problems, so what was meant to be a quiet year is now a big gap to fill. I have the space, a budget of about 12,000 euros for freight and mounting, and no show. I keep a list of candidates on the back of a receipt in my bag and cross them off in the evenings.

projects.name: Catalogue for the gallery's tenth year
projects.text: A small book with essays and photographs. The designer has finished the layout; the text is waiting on me. I keep telling myself it will come after the autumn show.

notes.text: The scaffolding is still on the building. Eleven months now. The façade restoration was supposed to finish in June. This morning a man in a hard hat dropped a bucket and the whole gallery shook. Inês says the light through the netting is "nice for photographs". I say it is nice for nobody.

Dinner with Ana, Teresa and old Zé at the fado house in Mouraria. Teresa sang, the first time in three years since her husband. Nobody said anything. We all looked at the tablecloth. Walked home along the Rua de São Tomé and cried a bit in the stairwell like a teenager.

Gonçalo is moving to Berlin on the 1st of October. He found a flat in Neukölln with two housemates and a shared bathroom the size of a wardrobe. I helped him sort his books. He took too many. I did not say anything. He is 26 and I keep wanting to tell him things about money.

Spent the whole afternoon trying to recompose the May slot in my head. The committee wants a name by December. An Andean group would have been perfect; the rest of the world gave me such a strange, difficult look when I mentioned that visas were the issue. I have a list: a Sami duodji group (but they showed in Porto last year), the Kuna molas (too well-known), Hmong story cloths (I do not know the community well enough). I do not want a show that looks like I am filling in. I want something that has a reason to exist.
A collector asked me why every label has a name and a village. "Is it not enough to say Peruvian?" I said: would you say "Italian" under a Caravaggio? She laughed. She bought the green mantle.
Paid the insurance quarterly. 612 euros. If the show in May is empty I will be paying that for nothing. Not nothing. But it feels like it.

The Chinchero belts arrived with one torn at the edge. The women had sewn a small repair patch with a note: "we are sorry, the donkey". I laughed in the customs office and the officer looked at me with real concern.
Dentist. A root canal on the upper left. I have decided to be brave and to treat it as meditation. It was not.
Gonçalo left this morning. We hugged in the station, awkward because of his enormous backpack. He said "do not worry, mãe". I said "I am not". We both knew.
Slept badly. Woke at four and looked at the ceiling. Thought about how many of the women whose names are on my walls have never seen the walls. One day I would like to bring one of them here.

messages.text: Inês: The printer says the labels will be ready Thursday but that he cannot do the 8pt font on the textured paper. Me: Then change the paper, not the font. Inês: He says it will cost 40 more. Me: Pay it.
Gonçalo: Mãe, do you have a spare suitcase? Me: The red one is in the back room. Gonçalo: It smells of camphor. Me: That is the smell of love. Gonçalo: That is the smell of 1998.

Sofia: Marta, we need a confirmation of your programme by 15 December. Without it we cannot give you the main street window. Me: Understood. I will send a concept by then. Sofia: We are sorry about the Andean group. Me: So am I. They are the ones who lost the most.
Teresa: Thank you for Saturday. I did not mean to make the table go quiet. Me: You did not. You made it go right. Teresa: Next time we drink more.

Carlos: The scaffolding company says another six weeks. Me: They said that in July. Carlos: I know. I am sorry. Me: Can we discuss a rent reduction for the months the entrance is blocked? Carlos: Let us talk after the autumn show.

constraints: Every maker must be named on the label and in any press material; no anonymous "folk art"
Will not ship fragile pieces without proper mounting or insurance
Cannot spend more than about 12,000 euros on the May show
Does not do commissions or work with sellers who cannot show provenance
